title: What xtpd is
summary: Every XTP node runs exactly one multi-threaded network service daemon, xtpd. It takes registrations, service requests and network infrastructure peerages, and runs the matching hooks. Applications never handle a carrier socket, key, route or firewall rule. It is also where the node decides what survives damage. Design doc: https://claude.ai/artifact/5xdnepoEfSABaQoCxcByNe Built so far: xtpd dev2, packages/oorexx_xtpd_v0.1-dev2 (bin/xtpd.rex, src/Xtpd.cls, libexec/xtp_roles.rex, libexec/ldap_role.rex; tests/run_all.sh). dev2 binds the bootstrap role file for grid item 1: a node catches up over xtp.roles and resolves LDAP.main by an authenticated ldap.role probe of a live LDAP server; READY only on FRESH. Rule found in dev2: no slow work under the Xtpd object guard, because the listener needs it (track) for every session.
authority: design (architecture Tom Dyer; written by Claude (Opus 5.5), 2026-11-24)
invariants: One xtpd per node; it is the node's only network process
Applications are hooks; they never hold a carrier socket, key, route or firewall rule
Nothing in this sphere is built or field-tested
procedure: Read xtpd.addressing before designing any XTP client or service
Read xtpd.decisions for what Tom has not yet decided

provenance.claim: XTP sessions: one context, both directions, per-direction close, one listener socket for all sessions
Service name to class to logical peer to route; IP addresses only in the route table; admission before CNTL

qualification_boundaries.status: dev1 and dev2 built: packages/oorexx_xtpd_v0.1-dev2 (Claude (Opus 5.5), 24-25 Nov 2026) - files, unix-socket OPEN with descriptor passing, exec hooks, the fence, receipts; dev2 adds the bootstrap role file (ChatGPT component xtpd_bootstrap v0.1-dev1): xtp.roles and ldap.role hooks, catch-up, READY only on FRESH, STATUS role and ROLE verb
qualification_boundaries.field: tested on loopback only (two daemons, UDP and raw IP 36, real OpenSSH and a real ooRexx LDAP server; 71 checks in the Ubuntu 22.04 build container as root; autobuild runs units only, as non-root); not field-tested; LDAP inputs, operating states, emergency files and announcements are not built
